summary.title: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents

details: Computer-use agents are bottlenecked by scarce human demonstration data for professional desktop applications; existing corpora are sparse screenshot-action pairs (largest open one, ScaleCUA, is ~2M screenshots ≈ <20h of 30fps video) that discard intermediate visual/kinematic dynamics.

CUA-Suite: an open ecosystem of human-collected desktop computer-use data built from one recording pipeline, whose core new artifact is VideoCUA — ~10K expert-designed tasks over 87 open-source desktop apps recorded as continuous, uncut 30fps screen video (~55h, ~6M frames) with millisecond-logged kinematic cursor/keystroke traces and multi-layered LLM-synthesized reasoning annotations (~497 words per step).

Design principle of universality: continuous video plus dense per-frame element annotations is a superset that can be losslessly converted into the screenshot-action, (s,a,s'), or continuous-trace formats required by existing agent frameworks.
Unified with two prior-released components from the same pipeline: UI-Vision (450-task grounding/planning benchmark) and GroundCUA (56K screenshots, 3.6M UI element bounding-box annotations).

87 open-source desktop apps across 12 categories (VS Code, Blender, Krita, Inkscape, LibreOffice, GnuCash, FreeCAD, OBS Studio, etc.), chosen for permissive licenses and UI similarity to closed-source counterparts.
Human experts author realistic tasks then execute them; 30fps uncut screen video plus millisecond-precision logs of clicks, drags, scrolls, keystrokes.

Keyframes taken immediately before state-changing actions; annotators draw bounding boxes for every visible UI element with text labels, PaddleOCR for long text, ~50% of elements tagged into 8 functional categories.
~70 professional annotators (India/Latin America, technical bachelor's degrees), 60–90 min per task, multi-tier QA plus author cross-checking.

Adopts OpenCUA's multi-layered trajectory synthesis with Claude-Sonnet-4.5 to produce per-step observation, thought/reasoning chain, action description, and reflection, alongside executable pyautogui code.
Average 496.7 words/step (157.4 observation, 194.3 reasoning, 17.7 action description, 127.4 reflection).
256 sampled VideoCUA tasks across 87 apps; after keyframe extraction and filtering of redundant moveTo→click pairs, 1,999 coordinate-based predictions (click, doubleClick, rightClick, dragTo).
Task-level setting: model gets the overall task instruction, last k=5 ground-truth actions as history, and current screenshot; no step-level instruction.
Metrics: mean/median pixel distance and success at 20px/50px thresholds; normalized coordinates converted to model input resolution.
Human study: 49 stratified-sampled tasks, 576 steps, annotators judge grounding correctness and action-type correctness (step correct only if both).
Action prediction: OpenCUA-7B and OpenCUA-32B (the publicly available foundation action models).

UI-Vision grounding leaderboard re-evaluation compiling reported numbers for MAI-UI-8B/32B, OpenCUA-7B/32B/72B, UI-Venus-Ground-7B/72B, PhiGround-7B (±o3 planner), UI-TARS-7B/72B, Qwen3-VL-8B/32B, InfiGUI-G1-7B, GUI-ARP-7B, HyperClick.

key_findings.finding: VideoCUA is the first large-scale, human-curated continuous-video desktop CUA corpus, exceeding the largest prior open dataset in video-equivalent scale.
key_findings.evidence: ~55 hours / ~6M frames of 30fps recordings over ~10K tasks and 87 apps, more than 2.5x ScaleCUA's ~2M screenshots (~18.5h at 30fps); the comparison table shows no prior dataset jointly offers continuous video, desktop focus, human curation, and long multi-layered CoT (Mind2Web, AgentTrek, AITW, GUI-Odyssey, OmniACT, VideoGUI ~7h, GUI-World ~83K frames, OpenCUA ~421K screenshots).

key_findings.finding: Current foundation action models fail on roughly 60% of professional desktop steps under realistic task-level prediction.
key_findings.evidence: On 256 tasks (1,999 coordinate predictions), OpenCUA-32B reaches 37.7% @50px (22.0% @20px, mean 274.2px, median 97px) and OpenCUA-7B only 16.5% @50px (mean 387.5px); human evaluation of the 32B model over 576 steps gives 57.6% stepwise accuracy.

key_findings.finding: The dominant failure mode is spatial grounding, not action-type selection.
key_findings.evidence: Human study decomposition: action-type correctness 85.9% (495/576) versus grounding accuracy 52.4% (195/372) on coordinate steps; non-coordinate steps (shortcuts, typing) score 67.6% (138/204); qualitative cases in Krita, FreeCAD, Inkscape, OBS show cross-panel confusion among visually similar elements.

key_findings.finding: Model reliability is strongly application-dependent, with canvas/creative tools hardest.
key_findings.evidence: Per-application @50px accuracy ranges from 3.6% to 73.3%; per-task human accuracy spans 0–100% (mean 56.2%), with 9/49 tasks above 80% and 7 below 30%.

key_findings.finding: On UI-Vision grounding, scores have roughly doubled in a year, but spatial-relation grounding remains the persistent gap, and reasoning/scale help.
key_findings.evidence: MAI-UI-32B sets 47.7% average (59.1 basic, 57.1 functional) versus prior SOTA UI-TARS-72B at 25.5%, yet best Spatial split score is only 26.9%; OpenCUA improves 29.7→37.3 from 7B to 72B, and adding an o3 planner to PhiGround-7B lifts average from 27.2 to 36.2.
